title: Dividing without div
description:
Do what GCC does: divide unsigned numbers by constants with `mul` and a magic number, **never** `div`. `mul rdi` multiplies `rax` by `rdi` into `rdx:rax`; the high half, `rdx`, is the product divided by 2⁶⁴.

| Function | Result | GCC's recipe |
|---|---|---|
| `udiv10(x)` | x ÷ 10 | high half of x × `0xCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCD`, then `shr` by 3 |
| `udiv3(x)` | x ÷ 3 | high half of x × `0xAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAB`, then `shr` by 1 |
| `urem10(x)` | x mod 10 | x − 10 × udiv10(x), with `lea` for the × 10 |
| `digit_sum(x)` | the sum of x's decimal digits | a loop using the udiv10 recipe |

All the numbers are unsigned 64-bit, including the largest, 18446744073709551615.

starter.solution.asm:
udiv10:
        xor     eax, eax
        ret

udiv3:
        xor     eax, eax
        ret

urem10:
        xor     eax, eax
        ret

digit_sum:
        xor     eax, eax
        ret

solution.solution.asm:
udiv10:
        mov     rax, 0xCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCD
        mul     rdi
        mov     rax, rdx
        shr     rax, 3
        ret

udiv3:
        mov     rax, 0xAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAB
        mul     rdi
        mov     rax, rdx
        shr     rax, 1
        ret

urem10:
        mov     rax, 0xCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCD
        mul     rdi
        shr     rdx, 3                  ; x / 10
        lea     rdx, [rdx + rdx*4]
        add     rdx, rdx                ; (x / 10) * 10
        mov     rax, rdi
        sub     rax, rdx
        ret

digit_sum:
        xor     ecx, ecx                ; the sum
        mov     r8, 0xCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCD
.loop:  test    rdi, rdi
        jz      .done
        mov     rax, r8
        mul     rdi
        shr     rdx, 3                  ; q = x / 10
        lea     rax, [rdx + rdx*4]
        add     rax, rax                ; q * 10
        sub     rdi, rax                ; the last digit
        add     rcx, rdi
        mov     rdi, rdx
        jmp     .loop
.done:  mov     rax, rcx
        ret

rules: No div: multiply by the magic number instead.
Use mul to get the high half.
